ddx.step1_summary:
- Chief complaint: Constant lower abdominal (suprapubic, midline) pain
- Symptom details: Began a few days ago; constant and worsening; severity ~8/10; localized below the umbilicus, midline; associated with light pink vaginal bleeding/spotting and slight vaginal discharge; nausea without vomiting; prior constipation last week (about 1 week duration) now resolved; currently eating/drinking and doing daily activities but pain is very uncomfortable
- Aggravating/alleviating factors: Not specified
- Gynecologic/obstetric: Sexually active (last intercourse ~4 days ago); contraceptive implant (Implanon/Nexplanon) inserted ~1 year ago; menses occur but irregular on implant; last menstrual period ~2–3 weeks ago; last pregnancy test ~1 month ago (no test since pain started); G0 (no prior pregnancies)
- Urinary: Denies dysuria, foul smell; frequency unclear; no flank pain reported
- GI: Constipation last week, now improved; no diarrhea; no blood in stool
- Constitutional: No reported fever, rigors, syncope, shoulder-tip pain, or dyspnea; mild nausea
- Past medical/surgical history: No surgeries; no chronic conditions reported
- Medications/allergies: Contraceptive implant; allergy to amoxicillin
- Family/social history: Lives with husband and his family; school teacher; smoking/alcohol unclear; no recreational drug use; no recent travel (last abroad ~1 year ago)
- Vitals/exam: Not available (teleconsultation; no physical exam performed)
- Labs/imaging: None obtained; advised to perform a pregnancy test today

V: Ovarian torsion: Acute pelvic pain due to compromised ovarian blood flow; classically unilateral and sudden, but severe pelvic pain could fit; less typical here due to midline location and gradual onset.
Ruptured/hemorrhagic ovarian cyst with intraperitoneal bleeding: Can cause acute pelvic pain and light bleeding; severity can be high; implant users can develop functional cysts.
I: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID): Lower abdominal/pelvic pain, abnormal bleeding/spotting, slight discharge, sexually active; lack of fever does not exclude PID.
Acute appendicitis: Worsening abdominal pain with nausea; early pain may be midline/periumbilical before localizing; absence of fever and RLQ localization argues against but does not exclude.
Urinary tract infection/cystitis: Suprapubic pain can occur; however, absence of dysuria, frequency, or fever makes this less likely.
Endometriosis (non-infectious inflammatory): Pelvic pain that may be cyclic; could present with spotting, but acute severe, constant pain over a few days is less typical.
N: Ovarian neoplasm with cystic degeneration: Can cause pelvic pain and irregular bleeding; less likely in a 23-year-old without mass symptoms.
Uterine fibroid (degenerating): May cause pelvic pain and abnormal bleeding; age and presentation make this less likely.
D: Constipation/IBS: Recent constipation could cause lower abdominal pain; symptoms have improved while pain persists, arguing against as sole cause.
I2: Implanon-related irregular bleeding and cramping: The implant commonly causes intermenstrual spotting and pelvic discomfort; may also be associated with functional ovarian cysts.
Medication allergy (amoxicillin): Not relevant to current presentation, but noted.
C: Müllerian duct anomaly: Could cause dysmenorrhea/abnormal bleeding; unlikely to newly present with acute severe pain.
T: Postcoital cervical/vaginal trauma: Recent intercourse 4 days ago with light pink spotting could be due to mucosal trauma; would not typically cause persistent severe pelvic pain.
E: Ectopic pregnancy: Pelvic pain and light vaginal bleeding; contraceptive implant reduces but does not eliminate pregnancy (and ectopic proportionally higher if pregnancy occurs); no recent pregnancy test since pain began.
Early intrauterine pregnancy with threatened miscarriage: Pelvic pain and spotting possible; timing relative to LMP (2–3 weeks) and implant use make this less likely but still important to exclude.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Sexually active woman with contraceptive implant, constant worsening pelvic pain and light vaginal bleeding; no pregnancy test since symptom onset. Implant failure is uncommon but ectopic must be ruled out urgently due to risk.
supporting_evidence: Lower abdominal/pelvic pain, constant and worsening
Light pink vaginal bleeding/spotting outside normal period
Sexually active; last intercourse ~4 days ago
No pregnancy test since pain began; last LMP ~2–3 weeks ago
opposing_evidence: Contraceptive implant markedly reduces pregnancy likelihood
No syncope, shoulder-tip pain, or hemodynamic instability reported
No known positive pregnancy test yet

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Common cause of pelvic pain in sexually active women; can present with abnormal bleeding and discharge even without fever.
supporting_evidence: Light vaginal bleeding and slight discharge
opposing_evidence: No fever or systemic symptoms reported
No pelvic exam performed to assess cervical motion or adnexal tenderness

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Functional ovarian cyst (including hemorrhagic/ruptured cyst), possibly associated with implant use
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Implant users can develop functional cysts; cysts can cause acute pelvic pain and irregular bleeding.
supporting_evidence: Implanon in situ; known association with functional ovarian cysts
opposing_evidence: Pain described as midline rather than unilateral (cysts often unilateral)
No sudden onset described (rupture often abrupt)
No ultrasound or exam to detect adnexal mass/tenderness

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Worsening abdominal pain with nausea; early appendicitis may present centrally before localizing. Lack of classic RLQ localization and fever lowers probability but does not exclude.
opposing_evidence: Pain primarily suprapubic/midline rather than RLQ

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Suprapubic pain can occur with cystitis, but absence of urinary symptoms makes this less likely.
